title: Water Leak Maintenance Log Form
subtitle: An original water leak workflow that carries planned or condition-based maintenance through safe release, with explicit qualified-review, stop-work, escalation, and accountable handoff controls.
description: A workflow-complete water leak maintenance log form for the suspected or confirmed water-release location that captures exact identity, domain observations, supporting evidence, decisions, exceptions, responsible owners, and closeout without replacing professional judgment or the organization's controlling procedures.
use_case: Use when service personnel need one record for maintenance trigger, asset baseline, work-control references, recurring events, readings, deferred defects, and qualified return-to-service approval. The leak response coordinator owns routing, and closure requires documented evidence, disposition of restrictions, and acceptance by the designated reviewer.

sections.title: Water leak maintenance log identity and ownership
sections.guidance: Define the maintained system, service interval, operating owner, and review period.

sections.title: Water leak asset baseline and maintenance readiness
sections.guidance: Reconcile the exact asset and known condition before maintenance or testing begins.

blocks.label: Planned maintenance task set
items: Confirm leak location, reporter, time, flow status, and affected areas
Screen electrical, structural, contamination, slip, and public hazards
Identify likely source without opening unsafe or unauthorized systems
Coordinate authorized shutoff and critical-service consequences
Record meter, flow, pressure, moisture, and visual evidence
Contain water and protect occupants or property within approved scope
Repair the confirmed source or route it to the correct qualified trade
Verify flow stopped and record post-repair or post-isolation readings
Assign drying, electrical, environmental, finish, and contents follow-up
Monitor for recurrence and document final service and property handoff

sections.title: Water leak work control and safe service boundary
sections.guidance: Record the qualified roles and controlling references; do not use this log as the controlling procedure.

blocks.label: Service readiness confirmations
items: Current procedure, manufacturer information, and applicable requirements were reviewed
Asset boundaries, every energy source, and affected systems were identified
Authorized, affected, contractor, and operations roles were coordinated
Isolation, stored-energy control, and verification references are complete
Required tools, instruments, parts, and protective controls are available
Test, temporary energization, and return-to-service steps have explicit authority
Customer, public, traffic, environmental, and critical-service impacts are controlled
Stop conditions and emergency escalation path are understood

blocks.label: Maintenance stop-work boundary
blocks.guidance: Do not enter water near electrical equipment, stand below a sagging ceiling, or handle suspected contaminated water. Keep occupants clear and use the organization's emergency route for rapid flooding, structural movement, gas odor, or critical-service impact. Only authorized personnel may operate shutoffs after evaluating downstream consequences. Maintenance stays restricted when isolation, stored energy, system condition, or work scope is unknown. Only the designated authorized person may direct changes to controls and the qualified release owner may approve return to service.

sections.title: Water leak maintenance events, condition, and readings
sections.guidance: Create a traceable history of work completed, condition found, evidence, and deferred action.

fields.label: Wear pattern, recurring fault, consumable trend, configuration change, and supporting evidence

sections.title: Water leak exceptions, stop conditions, and escalation
sections.guidance: Make every unresolved condition visible with an immediate control, owner, due point, and final disposition.

blocks.label: Stop-condition screen
items: Water contacting electrical equipment, outlets, panels, cords, or machinery
Bulging or sagging ceiling, unstable finish, structural movement, or falling material
Suspected sewage, chemical, fire-water, or other contaminated release
Rapid flooding, washout, sinkhole, severe pressure, or uncontrolled flow
Slip exposure, hidden opening, poor visibility, or unsafe access
Shutoff would impair fire protection, medical, process, or critical service
Gas odor, steam, hot water, refrigerant, or unknown fluid is also present
Condition exceeds responder authority, equipment, training, or protective controls
blocks.guidance: Check any condition observed or reported; checking an item does not mean the condition is controlled.

blocks.label: Qualified-person and stop-work boundary
blocks.guidance: Do not enter water near electrical equipment, stand below a sagging ceiling, or handle suspected contaminated water. Keep occupants clear and use the organization's emergency route for rapid flooding, structural movement, gas odor, or critical-service impact. Only authorized personnel may operate shutoffs after evaluating downstream consequences.

blocks.label: Exception and escalation register
blocks.guidance: Link each maintenance exception to supporting evidence and keep it open until disposition is recorded.

sections.title: Water leak decision, handoff, and accountable closeout
sections.guidance: Record the decision, remaining limitations, next action, and the people accountable for acceptance.

blocks.label: Closeout completeness
items: Suspected or confirmed water-release location identity and location were reconciled
Observed facts, measurements, and evidence references are complete
Decision authority and applicable review requirements were confirmed
Stop conditions, restrictions, and open exceptions remain visible
Customer, operations, or site handoff was recorded
Next action, owner, due point, and record-retention route are explicit

fields.label: Limitations, assumptions, restrictions, customer message, and next-action context

blocks.label: Accountable review and handoff
blocks.guidance: Signatures acknowledge the recorded decision and handoff; they do not waive unresolved restrictions.
